cards.front: What is the activation function $\mathrm{ReLU}(x)$ and why is it used in deep neural networks?
cards.back: $\mathrm{ReLU}(x)=\max(0,x)$. It is used to introduce non-linearity (a piecewise linear function) into the network, because a purely linear matrix multiplication is insufficient for learning complex patterns.

cards.front: In machine learning, what is the difference between training data and test data?
cards.back: Training data is used to optimize the matrix weights (parameters) of the model. Test data is unseen data used to evaluate how well the model generalizes to new inputs.

cards.front: How do you calculate the variance of a centered data vector $v$ (where the mean is already $0$) as a pure dot product?
cards.back: The variance corresponds to the dot product of the vector with itself: $v^T v$.

cards.front: How do you calculate the covariance of two centered data vectors $v_1$ and $v_2$ as a pure dot product?
cards.back: The covariance corresponds to the mixed dot product of the two vectors: $v_1^T v_2$.

cards.front: What two special mathematical properties does a covariance matrix $C$ built from real data always have?
cards.back: It is always symmetric ($C=C^T$) and positive semi-definite (all eigenvalues satisfy $\lambda_i \ge 0$).
